headline: LLM agents orchestrate domain tools for modeling, statistics, and prediction, with human review calibrating errors
label: Llm Agents For Biological Workflows
summary: Preprints test LLM orchestration of established biological tools, reporting accuracy and review-burden trade-offs in modeling, omics statistics, and complex stoichiometry.
synthesis: The dominant thread is LLMs acting as orchestrators over established computational biology tools rather than as standalone predictors. Octomod coordinates AMICI, pyPESTO, SBML and PEtab for mechanistic model construction and hypothesis testing. statLens combines LLMs, code and human review for omics statistics, reporting 92.5-95.0% accuracy. StoiAgent integrates sequence, structural, AlphaFold3 and literature evidence for stoichiometry prediction. The ECS framework quantifies human oversight, with 5% residual error at 44.6% review in myeloma simulations. A comparison of orchestrators finds local Gemma 4 matches larger models on single-turn tasks but lags on multi-turn ones. The review on foundation-model knowledge boundaries frames these limits. What is new is explicit reporting of oversight cost and orchestrator capability, not new core algorithms.
